note: Engineering bounds of the extraction service and its benches, each with where its value comes from. Decision thresholds are fitted separately (params.json).

generate_budget.provenance: cap on generated tokens per generate op; bounds one request's latency and KV memory on a 16 GB machine; not a quality parameter

quote_context.provenance: code points of prefix/suffix in a TextQuoteSelector; W3C Web Annotation leaves the length to the producer; long enough to disambiguate a repeated quote in the fixture, not fitted

socket_read_bytes.provenance: Unix-socket read chunk; any size is correct, this one reads a typical request in one call

jevk5_option_budget.provenance: measured: ollaya refuses a jevk5 choice with more than 16 options ('options do not fit the option budget')

encoder_device.provenance: measured 2026-10-21 on the slice: footprint cpu fp32 2313->2427 MB, cpu half 2005->2044 MB, mps fp32 3142->3258 MB, mps half 3147->3979 MB; identical entity precision/recall (0.848/0.966) in all four

encoder_half.provenance: same measurement: half precision on cpu is the smallest footprint with no loss of a gold mention

time_window_days.provenance: days either side of a source's anchor day offered as TIMEX3 DATE candidates; three weeks covers 'in two weeks' and 'last Friday' style expressions in the fixture; a starting point to fit against labelled time decisions, not fitted

socket_backlog.provenance: pending connections the kernel holds before accept; each accepted connection is read on its own thread at once, so this only bounds a burst
